notes: No graded rule changed. git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ touches only Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern (new paragraphs on body patterns, dot chains, get_in/1 and Map.fetch/2), In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use (rewritten), and the capture_log section of ex_unit.md. None is in this case's row of the rule index, so all ten listed rules are graded to the 2026-10-22-d standard. The caller's request to count violations per sentence bullet applies to evals/cases/webhook-parser.md and evals/cases/library-client.md; evals/cases/rate-limiter.md has no such bullets, so there are no per-sentence counts for this case.

Changed rules seen outside the list: under the current Read required keys text, haiku-1 line 202 reads a required key with brackets (decoded["default_limit"]) and is listed in other_violations, as earlier sweeps listed string-key bracket reads. The new body-pattern sentence ("A pattern in a body that pulls one atom key or struct field out of a value the function already holds, with no literal and no guard, is dot access written long.") catches nothing: every body pattern is on a call's result (opus-1 line 73, sonnet-1 line 132). The rewritten head-binding rule catches nothing: no function with two or more clauses binds a field its patterns and guards do not use.

Designs. Opus-1 is the only run that moved counts out of a GenServer: callers insert one row per request into a public ordered_set ETS table owned by the GenServer, count with :ets.select_count/2 and delete their row when over the limit (lines 79-89), the pattern processes.md names; the table and limits are found through :persistent_term keyed by the limiter's name. The other four keep every count in one GenServer's state behind GenServer.call, so Pick the abstraction and Use ETS are violated in haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2, and haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 say so in their moduledocs. Haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-1 use top-level module names (RateLimiter, RateLimit, RateLimit). Every run reads its JSON limits file inside init/1; as in 2026-10-22-d, that misses the case check but decides no verdict. All five accept :name.

With rule: haiku-1 and haiku-2 violate it through else blocks. Haiku-1's load_config/1 (lines 200-208) has a no-op {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason} and a _ -> {:error, :invalid_format} that relabels the %{} mismatch of step 2; haiku-2's load_limits/1 (lines 164-170) relabels the File.read/1 error in else ({:error, reason} when is_atom(reason) -> {:error, {:file, reason}}) and holds a no-op clause. Sonnet-2's four-step with (lines 125-130) has no else and private step functions, so it is clean. Opus-1 and sonnet-1 have no with.

Comments: sonnet-2 is violated because its public start_link/1 (line 53) has no @doc, as earlier sweeps counted an undocumented public function. Section labels (## Client API, # Helpers and similar) are not counted, as before. Two one-line comments above private functions are counted clean but are close calls: haiku-2 line 154 (# Timestamps are kept newest first. Keep only those inside the rolling window.) and sonnet-1 line 198 (# Drops timestamps that have left the window.). Each summarizes a defp, which cannot carry @doc, and haiku-2's first sentence states an ordering the code cannot show; a stricter reading would count sonnet-1 line 198 as restating prune/2.

Verification, in scratch copies under the grading scratch folder. mix format --check-formatted passes for opus-1 and haiku-2 and fails for haiku-1 (line 131, 116 characters), sonnet-1 (line 174, 117) and sonnet-2 (lines 49 and 96, 116 and 106). No session ran mix format. The limiter modules compile with elixirc --warnings-as-errors in all five (opus-1 and sonnet-2 with the Plug example modules cut off, since Plug is not installed). In every run a 50-task concurrent burst admitted exactly 2 for a user at the default limit of 2 and 5 for user 42 configured at 5, and a second instance under name: :other admitted 2 of 50. Haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 convert ids with to_string/1, so 1 and "1" share a count; opus-1 keys by the raw id, so "1" got its own 2 after 1 was exhausted.
All five runs have rc 0, a model_id matching their tier and empty reads; no session called the Skill tool. Expected reads (processes.md) is unmet in all five, as expected for baseline runs.
